notes: About 19:00 Kraiss reported a hopeless situation to Marcks and was ordered to withdraw far to the south to a new line along the Elle River from Berigny to Airel (about ten miles), moving in darkness and finishing by 06:00 on 10 June; for that line he had 2,500 men, 14 artillery pieces, 16 antiaircraft guns and 5 tanks (CMH). Night 9/10 June the division retired toward Saint-Lô, opening the Caumont gap. The point is the midpoint of the ordered line, not a position held on the day: on 9 June the division was still pulling out of the Aure/Trévières front. The 2,500 figure is the strength CMH gives for holding the new line and is not a count of the whole division; strength is therefore heavily_depleted relative to the division's size, and by 16-17 June CMH calls the division only a Kampfgruppe of about regimental strength (see C0127). Establishment figures conflict by source and basis and are kept as sourced, not reconciled: Wikipedia's 352nd Division page gives about 17,200 at full strength on the old-type establishment (10,971-17,200 depending on battalion size); Wikipedia's Normandy landings page gives a full-strength unit of around 12,000.
